purpose: How a working gold-plating bench keeps the people in it alive and unharmed: naming the hazard classes actually present in the room (cyanide-bearing solutions, mineral acids, caustic alkalis, nickel salts, hot tanks and stored electrical energy), holding the cyanide/acid segregation line as a physical property of the premises rather than a behaviour, deriving storage, labeling, ventilation, monitoring and PPE obligations from the product's own safety data sheet and the local jurisdiction's rules, proving spill and exposure readiness by drill rather than by intention, recording who is trained and authorized to do what, and running every job through a readiness gate that fails closed when throughput and safety meet.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the shop runs purchased commercial plating chemistry handled per its supplier safety data sheet and technical data sheet; no bath is formulated from raw chemicals

at least one chemistry family in use may be cyanide-bearing (alkaline gold cyanide strike and build, cyanide copper strike) while acids are present for pickling and activation, so the segregation obligation is live rather than hypothetical
the bench is a small shop or one-person operation without an in-house safety department; obligations are met with modest equipment, written records, outside training and supplier support

every exposure limit, quantity threshold, licence condition and ventilation requirement is jurisdiction-specific and dated; this knowledge base carries obligation classes and verification pointers, never compliance numbers
safety and compliance outrank throughput, cost and customer deadline wherever they meet, and the decision to decline or outsource a job is always available
exclusions: what leaves the shop: rinse waters, spent baths, filters and sludges as regulated waste classes, waste characterization, manifests and licensed handlers, drag-out reduction economics, precious-metal reclaim accounting, and discharge or air-permit rules belong to the sibling waste and environmental handling knowledge base; this knowledge base stops at containing and segregating material inside the premises and hands the stream over at the door

what you may call the finished piece: 'gold plated', 'vermeil', 'gold filled' and 'rolled gold' as regulated term classes, thickness and karat thresholds, nickel-release limits for skin-contact goods, durability advertising and claim record trails belong to the sibling marking, claims and consumer rules knowledge base

being the training: this knowledge base names obligation classes and points at formal hazardous-material, chemical-handling and workplace-safety training delivered by qualified providers; it is not that training, not a certificate, and never a step-by-step handling procedure for a named product

asserted numeric limits: exposure limits, storage quantity thresholds, licensing conditions, capture velocities and discharge limits are jurisdiction-specific and change; verify each with your own workplace and hazardous-material authority and record the date, because nothing here is a compliance figure

medical advice of any kind: exposure management, antidote provision and use, nickel-allergy diagnosis and fitness-to-work decisions belong to emergency services, a physician and occupational health; the shop's role is accurate information handover, never diagnosis or treatment

bath performance and process outcome: temperature, gold concentration, current density, time, deposit quality, adhesion, colour and run scheduling belong to the bath chemistry, surface preparation, process execution and quality specialists; safety touches a process parameter only where that parameter is itself a hazard control, such as the alkaline pH floor of a free-cyanide solution or the ban on air agitation

do-it-yourself bath formulation from raw chemicals, improvised neutralization recipes, and any suggestion that a careful procedure can substitute for physical segregation, source extraction or gas detection
sewer or general-refuse disposal advice in any form, and legal advice in any form; regulated-waste routing and legal sign-off are named as escalations, not answered here

competency_questions.question: Can I actually run this chemistry in the room I have, or is the honest answer a cyanide-free system or sending the work to a licensed plater?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SAFETY_MANDATE_FRAME lists the obligation classes each chemistry family triggers and states the decline-or-outsource option, VENTILATION_OBLIGATION supplies the source-extraction test the premises must pass, and SAFETY_READINESS_GATE states that partial controls never license a run

competency_questions.question: Which authorities actually govern my bench, and who do I have to ask before I buy a cyanide-bearing product?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: JURISDICTION_RULE_MAP names the rule classes, their owning authority, the proof document and the verification date, and STORAGE_AND_SECURITY_CLASSES states that quantity and security conditions are read from that register rather than assumed

competency_questions.question: What exactly makes a cyanide gold bath dangerous, and which ordinary bench actions release the gas?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CYANIDE_HAZARD_CLASS names the inhalation, dermal and ingestion routes, the acid-contact gas mechanism and the falling-pH mechanism, and PH_FLOOR_DISCIPLINE explains the one-way drift that walks a bath towards that floor between runs

competency_questions.question: How do I lay the room out so acid and cyanide can never meet, in a tank, on a tool, or in a spill?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CYANIDE_ACID_SEGREGATION states the never-mixed, never-co-stored, never-shared-drain line and its equipment and routing consequences, and ZONE_DRAIN_AND_CONTAINMENT proves where each zone's worst credible spill ends up

competency_questions.question: How must I store and secure what I hold, and what has to carry a label?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STORAGE_AND_SECURITY_CLASSES gives the incompatibility and access-control classes, LABELING_AND_DECANT_DISCIPLINE requires an identity on every vessel including rinses and drag-out, and CHEMICAL_REGISTER supplies the quantity and location picture the storage plan is sized against

competency_questions.question: What ventilation and gas monitoring am I obliged to have, and how do I know they still work today?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VENTILATION_OBLIGATION distinguishes source capture from room dilution and names its verification routine, and GAS_DETECTION_AND_ALARM gives the bump-test, calibration and end-of-life discipline plus the leave-do-not-investigate response rule

competency_questions.question: What protective equipment does this specific task need, how do I decide, and when do I refuse the job outright?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PPE_SELECTION_AND_CARE derives glove, eye, face and body protection from the product's safety data sheet rather than habit and states the no-equipment-no-job rule, and SDS_TDS_LIBRARY makes that sheet reachable from the bench

competency_questions.question: Who is allowed to do this work, what training must they hold first, and may they do it alone?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPETENCY_AND_AUTHORIZATION requires external formal training as a prerequisite, per-task in-shop sign-off, a named authorization list and the no-lone-working rule for free-cyanide work, and WRITTEN_SAFE_WORK_INSTRUCTIONS puts the authorized method at the bench in dated form

competency_questions.question: A bottle just went over, or a bath splashed on someone — what happens in the first two minutes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SPILL_RESPONSE_READINESS gives the zone-kit and size-decision rule with evacuation as the first branch in the cyanide zone, EYEWASH_AND_SHOWER_READINESS gives the immediate flush and its reachability test, and EXPOSURE_RESPONSE_AND_MEDICAL_ROUTING gives the remove-flush-call sequence

competency_questions.question: What am I obliged to tell emergency responders, and where does a health worry like a rash after a nickel run go?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EXPOSURE_RESPONSE_AND_MEDICAL_ROUTING requires naming the chemical to responders and handing over the safety data sheet and routes all personal symptoms to professional care, NICKEL_SENSITIZER_CLASS explains why a rash is an occupational-health referral and not a shop diagnosis, and SIGNAGE_AND_DRILL_PROGRAM puts the hazard information where responders will find it

competency_questions.question: How do I stop the corrosive and hot-tank hazards from being the injury that actually happens in a shop that never touches cyanide?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACID_ALKALI_CORROSIVE_CLASS names the burn, splash, fume and dilution-order hazards, HOT_SOLUTION_AND_ENERGY_HAZARDS names the hot-tank, heater, gas-evolution and wet-electrical hazards, and EYEWASH_AND_SHOWER_READINESS supplies the response those two classes are sized against

competency_questions.question: What has to be true before I start a run today, and who is allowed to stop it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SAFETY_READINESS_GATE lists the pre-run items, states that the gate fails closed and names the halt authority, and INCIDENT_AND_NEAR_MISS_LEARNING shows how a failed gate item becomes a logged control failure rather than a private workaround

competency_questions.question: What do I do with a container nobody recognizes, or a chemical whose safety data sheet I cannot find?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SDS_TDS_LIBRARY makes an unobtainable sheet a purchase-and-use blocker, LABELING_AND_DECANT_DISCIPLINE explains how the unknown vessel is created and forbidden, and CHEMICAL_REGISTER supplies the provenance trail used to identify it without opening or testing it

glossary.definition: The rapidly-acting toxic gas liberated when a cyanide-bearing solution or salt meets acid, or when a free-cyanide solution's pH falls far enough; published plating chemistry places the practical alkaline floor for free-cyanide solutions around pH 10.5, which is why the alkaline condition of the bath is a life-safety control and not a process preference.

The European hazard statement class 'contact with acids liberates very toxic gas' that appears on cyanide-bearing products; on a plating bench it is the label-level statement of the segregation rule that governs the whole room.

The excess cyanide deliberately present in an alkaline gold or copper bath beyond what is bound in the metal complex; it is what keeps the bath stable and what makes the solution, its rinses and its drag-out acutely hazardous rather than merely regulated.

The film of bath solution a piece and its rack carry out of the tank into the next vessel; in safety terms it is the mechanism that turns a bucket of apparently clean rinse water into a cyanide-bearing solution that must be treated exactly like the bath.

The supplier's hazard document for a specific product, carrying hazard classification, incompatibilities, protective-equipment guidance, first-aid and spill sections; it is the governing text from which this shop's controls for that product are derived, and it is handed to responders in an emergency.

The supplier's operating document for a specific product, carrying its working window and maintenance instructions; setpoints come from here and from the shop's own logged runs, never from a general knowledge base, and the safety-relevant limits it names (such as an alkaline floor) are read as hard constraints.

Extraction that captures mist and vapour at the tank before it reaches the operator's breathing zone, as opposed to a room fan or open window that merely dilutes and redistributes; the obligation class, its verification interval and any airflow requirement are set by the local workplace authority.

A short functional check that exposes a gas detector to a known challenge to confirm it responds and alarms, distinct from a full calibration; an alarm device that has never been bump-tested provides reassurance rather than protection.

A tray, bund or kerbed area that holds the contents of the largest credible container failure in a zone so a spill cannot travel, reach a drain, or cross into an incompatible zone; it is the physical answer to the question of where a fallen vessel's contents would go.

The unit this knowledge base is written in: a named duty a shop must satisfy continuously (segregate, store, label, extract, monitor, protect, train, be ready, record) paired with a pointer to the document or authority that fixes its enforceable detail in this jurisdiction, deliberately stated without an invented number.

nodes.definition: Settle, before a single tank is filled, what the safety layer of a plating bench actually is: a standing set of obligation classes — segregate, store, label, extract, monitor, protect, train, be ready, record — that the shop must satisfy continuously for as long as the chemistry is in the building, plus the standing rule that these obligations outrank throughput, cost and the customer's date every time they meet. The frame also fixes what this knowledge is not: it is class-level discipline plus a pointer to formal hazardous-material and workplace-safety training and to the shop's own jurisdiction, never a substitute for either and never an improvised handling procedure for a named product. The decision it produces is blunt and is made per chemistry family: this room can host it under these controls, or it cannot and the honest move is a lower-hazard system or sending the plating out to a licensed shop.

included: the obligation-class vocabulary the whole knowledge base is written in
the safety-beats-throughput dominance statement
the per-chemistry-family run-here, substitute or outsource decision
the explicit training-pointer boundary
excluded: step-by-step handling procedure for a named product, which comes from the safety data sheet and formal training
waste characterization and disposal routing, which is the waste knowledge base
marking and advertising claims, which is the marking knowledge base

pros.claim: Deciding the safety frame before buying chemistry stops a shop owning a hazard it has no way to control
pros.example: a bench jeweller works through the obligation classes for alkaline gold cyanide, concludes a shared residential garage with no source extraction and no second trained person cannot host it, and buys a cyanide-free system instead of a drum of potassium cyanide

pros.claim: A single dominance statement written where the schedule is set removes the daily argument about whether a control can slip for one job
pros.example: the rule that a failed readiness item stops the run is pinned next to the job board, so the ring order due Friday is rescheduled rather than run with the extraction fan out of service

cons.claim: An obligation-class frame is deliberately non-numeric, so it tells the shop a control is required without telling it what will satisfy an inspector
cons.example: the frame establishes that source extraction is obligatory but the enforceable capture requirement and its test interval come from the local workplace regulator, not from here

cons.claim: Framing safety as a set of classes can read as bureaucracy to a one-person shop and be quietly reduced to a folder nobody opens
cons.example: the classes are written up once at start-up and never revisited when a second bench and a nickel line are added two years later

failure_modes: treating safety as an appendix to the process sheet instead of the gate the process passes through
reading class-level obligations as a complete working procedure and skipping the formal training they point at
letting a customer deadline or a gold-price window reorder the dominance rule for one job
never using the decline-or-outsource option, so the shop runs chemistry its premises cannot support
acceptance_tests: for every chemistry family the shop intends to run, the obligation classes it triggers are listed and each is marked satisfied, not yet satisfied, or unsatisfiable in these premises
the safety-beats-throughput rule appears where jobs are scheduled, not only in a binder, and names who may halt a run
at least one documented instance exists of a job or a chemistry being declined or outsourced on safety grounds
revisit_triggers: a new chemistry family or product class is introduced
the premises change: a new room, a shared building, a residential address, or a landlord alteration
headcount changes, including taking on a first employee or an apprentice
an incident or near miss shows an obligation class was never really satisfied

base.update_signal: the shop changes premises, chemistry family or headcount, or the workplace regulator issues guidance that adds or reshapes an obligation class

nodes.definition: Build and keep current a register of which authorities actually govern this bench and what each one owns, holding pointers and dates rather than remembered numbers: the workplace-safety regulator for exposure limits, risk assessment and training duty; poisons or precursor licensing for cyanide salts and gold cyanide purchase; the fire and building authority for stored quantities, cabinets and separation distances; the drainage and environmental authority whose rules the waste specialist executes; and the landlord and insurer conditions that in practice bite a small shop before any regulator does. Each entry names the rule class, the office or person to ask, the document that would prove compliance, and the date it was last verified — because every figure in this space is jurisdiction-specific and dated, and a stale answer quoted confidently is a compliance failure that looks exactly like compliance.

included: the register of rule classes with owning authority, proof document and verification date
landlord and insurer conditions as first-order constraints
the escalation to a qualified professional when a rule class is ambiguous
the re-verification interval that keeps the register from silently ageing
excluded: asserting any numeric limit, quantity threshold or licence condition as a universal fact
waste manifesting and discharge mechanics, which belong to the waste knowledge base
product marking and advertising rules, which belong to the marking knowledge base
legal advice; the register points at the authority, it does not interpret law for the shop

pros.claim: A dated pointer register turns the unanswerable question of whether something is legal into a short list of named offices to call
pros.example: before ordering potassium gold cyanide the shop can show which licensing office it asked, what it was told, and on what date

pros.claim: Recording landlord and insurer conditions alongside statutory ones catches the constraint that most often shuts a small plating bench
pros.example: the lease excludes hazardous processes and the insurer excludes cyanide operations, which settles the chemistry choice before any regulator is involved

cons.claim: The register goes stale silently: nothing in the shop signals that a threshold moved at the last licence renewal
cons.example: a storage quantity condition tightened when the licence was reissued and the cabinet limit on the wall still shows the old figure

cons.claim: Getting authoritative answers costs calendar time a job-driven shop rarely budgets, which tempts substitution of forum answers
cons.example: a licensing office takes weeks to respond and the shop proceeds on a plating-forum post from another country

failure_modes: copying another jurisdiction's threshold into the shop file because it was easier to find
treating a supplier sales answer or a forum post as the regulatory answer
recording an answer without its date, so an old ruling is quoted as current
mapping only the statutory authorities and missing the landlord, insurer or building conditions
acceptance_tests: every rule class in the register names an authority, a proof document and a verification date
no numeric threshold appears anywhere in the shop's documents without its source and the date it was confirmed
the register names, for each unresolved question, who will be asked and by when
revisit_triggers: licence renewal, inspection, or any contact from an authority
a supplier reports a change in a product's control or classification status
the shop moves, sublets, or adds an operation such as a nickel line
the oldest verification date in the register passes the shop's stated re-check interval

base.update_signal: an authority publishes a change, a licence is renewed or inspected, or the register's oldest verification date passes the shop's re-check interval

nodes.definition: Treat the safety data sheet and the technical data sheet of every purchased product as the governing text for that product, and keep them as a live library rather than a drawer: a current sheet on file for every chemical in the building, in the working language of whoever is on shift, matched to the supplier's latest revision, indexed to the container it describes, and physically reachable from the room where the chemical is used rather than from an office computer. The safety data sheet is where the hazard classification, incompatibilities, glove and breathing guidance, first-aid steps and spill instructions come from, so it is the parent of nearly every control in this knowledge base; the technical data sheet carries the operating window, including the safety-relevant limits such as an alkaline floor. The discipline it enforces is simple and unpopular: nobody settles a glove, a compatibility or a first-aid question from memory.

included: acquiring, versioning and indexing sheets to containers
floor-level accessibility during an incident
extracting hazard, incompatibility, protection and first-aid content into the shop's own controls
the rule that an unobtainable sheet blocks purchase and use
excluded: formulating a bath from raw chemicals, which is outside this program entirely
restating setpoints as universal values; the specific product's sheet governs its own window
treating a sheet as a substitute for formal training or for supervised practice

pros.claim: One governing document per product ends the argument about glove material, incompatibility and first aid before it starts
pros.example: the protection section of the sheet for an acid stripper, not shop habit, decides that a thin examination glove is not acceptable for decanting it

pros.claim: Sheets kept at the point of use are also the document handed to paramedics and firefighters, which changes the quality of the response
pros.example: a splash victim leaves for hospital with the printed sheet naming the actual product rather than a description of a yellow liquid

cons.claim: Sheet quality varies and generic phrasing can under-specify what the bench actually needs
cons.example: a sheet advises 'suitable protective gloves' with no material or breakthrough guidance, forcing a written query to the supplier before the product is used

cons.claim: Maintaining currency across every product is real recurring administration that small shops routinely let slide
cons.example: a reformulated brightener arrives with a new revision and the folder still holds the sheet from three years ago

failure_modes: a container arriving and entering service with no sheet filed at all
an outdated revision that predates a reformulation and misstates the hazard
the library held in an office or a cloud account nobody can reach during a splash
sheets filed in a language the person on shift cannot read
acceptance_tests: every container in the chemical register maps to a current safety data sheet, and every plating chemistry additionally maps to its technical data sheet
an operator standing at the tanks can produce the sheet for any vessel in the room within about a minute, with the power off
no product is in use whose sheet could not be obtained; unobtainable means not purchased
revisit_triggers: a supplier reissues or reformulates a product
a new product enters the shop or an existing one changes supplier
a decanted vessel is found whose parent document cannot be traced
the person on shift changes and the working language of the library no longer matches

base.update_signal: a supplier issues a new sheet revision, a product changes, or an audit of the library finds a container without a current matched sheet

nodes.definition: Keep a written register of what hazardous material is actually in the building: which product, in what quantity band, in which container, in which zone, under whose control — and crucially including the vessels people forget are chemicals because they look like water, namely the working tanks, the rinse cascade and the static drag-out bucket that holds bath solution by design. Quantity matters because storage, licensing and fire obligations are quantity-banded in most jurisdictions, and because emergency responders entering the room need to know what is present and how much. The register is also the shop's honest total of cyanide-bearing solution on site, which is the number that decides whether its controls are proportionate or merely well-intentioned, and it is reconciled by walking the room rather than by reading last year's list.

included: container-level inventory with quantity band, location, hazard class and responsible person
tanks, rinses and drag-out vessels counted as inventory
a reconciliation walk-round on a stated cadence
the total cyanide-bearing volume as a single stated figure for the premises
excluded: characterizing and manifesting material once it becomes waste, which is the waste knowledge base
bath analysis, replenishment and dump decisions, which belong to the bath chemistry specialist
asserting the local quantity threshold at which a licence, cabinet or notification becomes required

pros.claim: A container-level register makes hidden inventory visible, and hidden inventory is where small shops are surprised
pros.example: the walk-round shows the unlabelled static drag-out bucket behind the bench holds more cyanide-bearing solution than the strike tank it serves

pros.claim: A single stated on-site quantity is the number every other obligation is sized against, from cabinet capacity to responder notification
pros.example: the total litres of acid on site turns out to exceed the corrosive cabinet's capacity, which caps future order sizes

cons.claim: A register is a snapshot and starts drifting the moment a delivery arrives or a bath is made up
cons.example: two litres of hydrochloric acid are delivered on a busy Friday, stood on the floor, and never entered

cons.claim: Quantity banding is only meaningful against local thresholds the shop must verify separately, so the register alone answers no compliance question
cons.example: the register shows the litres held but the cabinet and notification thresholds still have to come from the jurisdiction register

failure_modes: counting labelled shelf stock only and ignoring tanks, rinses and drag-out
recording quantity once at start-up and never reconciling it against the room
no responsible person named, which in a shared building means nobody owns the risk
keeping the register only in the owner's head, where responders cannot read it
acceptance_tests: a walk-round reconciles the register against every vessel in the room, including rinse and drag-out containers, on the shop's stated cadence
the register states a current total for cyanide-bearing solution and for acids held on site
each entry names a location, a quantity band and a responsible person
revisit_triggers: any delivery, bath make-up, bath dump or product substitution
a change of zone layout that moves where material lives
an inspection, insurer visit or responder pre-notification
the readiness gate finds a vessel that is not in the register

base.update_signal: a reconciliation walk-round finds material not on the register, or a delivery, dump or layout change alters what is held

nodes.definition: Hold an exact picture of what a cyanide-bearing plating solution is, because every downstream control is non-negotiable only if this picture is understood. Potassium gold cyanide, the free potassium or sodium cyanide that stabilises an alkaline gold or copper bath, and every rinse and drag-out vessel that has touched them carry acute toxicity by inhalation, skin and ingestion routes; they liberate hydrogen cyanide gas on contact with any acid, which is the hazard statement printed on the label and the reason the segregation line exists; they evolve that gas without any acid addition if the solution's pH falls far enough, with published plating chemistry putting the practical alkaline floor for free-cyanide solutions around pH 10.5; they become an inhalation route when agitation aerosolises them, which is why air sparging into these baths is not done; and they are acutely toxic to aquatic life, which is why the stream leaving the shop is a regulated-waste question, never a drain question.

included: the three exposure routes including dermal absorption
the acid-contact gas mechanism and the falling-pH gas mechanism
mist and aerosol as an inhalation route and the consequent agitation restriction
the rule that rinses and drag-out inherit the hazard of the bath
excluded: cyanide destruction chemistry, treatment and disposal routing, which is the waste knowledge base
medical management of an exposed person, which belongs to emergency services and physicians
bath performance questions such as what free cyanide does to throwing power or deposit purity

pros.claim: Naming the mechanisms lets an operator recognise hazards the container label does not shout about
pros.example: the third rinse bucket is handled, stored and disposed of as a cyanide-bearing solution because drag-out made it one

pros.claim: Understanding that gas can appear from pH drift alone, with no acid anywhere, converts pH from a process reading into a safety reading
pros.example: a Monday-morning pH check on a bath left standing over a weekend is treated as a safety check before the lid is lifted

cons.claim: Hazard-class knowledge is not handling competence and can breed a dangerous confidence in someone who has only read about it
cons.example: an operator who can recite the acid-contact statement still must not open a cyanide container before supervised formal training

cons.claim: The class picture is qualitative by design, so it cannot tell a shop what airborne concentration is acceptable in its jurisdiction
cons.example: the exposure limit that a workplace inspector will measure against comes from the regulator, not from this description

failure_modes: treating dilute rinse water as harmless because it looks like water
assuming the hazard is only inhalation and handling solutions with inadequate skin protection
aerating or air-sparging a bath for better agitation and creating a mist exposure route
believing a sealed pen-plating or ready-made product cannot present the same class of hazard
acceptance_tests: the operator can state the exposure routes and both gas-generation mechanisms without consulting a document
every vessel that has contacted a cyanide-bearing solution is identified in the register and treated at the same hazard level as the bath
no agitation method in use aerosolises a cyanide-bearing bath
revisit_triggers: a new cyanide-bearing product or a different gold system enters the shop
an agitation, heating or filtration change alters how the bath surface behaves
the supplier issues a revised hazard classification
an alarm, odour report or symptom suggests an unrecognised release path

base.update_signal: a supplier revises the hazard classification of a product in use, or a release path is discovered that the current picture does not explain

nodes.definition: Give the corrosives the seriousness they earn, because in a shop that never touches cyanide they are what actually injures people: hydrochloric pickle that fumes and attacks eyes, airways and every steel tool within reach; sulfuric acid whose dilution is strongly exothermic so acid always goes into water and never the reverse; caustic soak cleaners and hot alkaline baths whose splash risk to the eyes is the classic blinding injury of plating rooms; and the second-order effect that acid fume quietly corrodes the equipment the safety case depends on, so a rusted extraction damper or a seized cabinet latch is a corrosive-hazard symptom rather than a maintenance annoyance. Their controls overlap with the cyanide controls but are not identical, and treating them as the minor hazard is how a shop with an excellent cyanide plan still ends up in an emergency department.

included: skin, eye and airway injury routes for acids and alkalis
the exothermic-dilution order rule
hot alkaline splash as a distinct severity class
fume damage to safety-critical equipment as a monitored consequence
excluded: choosing pickle chemistry, strength or dump criteria, which belong to surface preparation and bath chemistry
spent pickle liquor disposal, which is the waste knowledge base
any improvised neutralization recipe

pros.claim: Treating corrosives as first-class hazards fixes the injuries that are statistically most likely on a small bench
pros.example: a face shield becomes standard for lifting work out of a hot alkaline cleaner, not just for cyanide work

pros.claim: Watching fume damage gives an early, visible indicator that containment and extraction are degrading
pros.example: rust blooming on tools and hinges near the pickle tank prompts an extraction check before anyone is overexposed

cons.claim: Familiarity breeds shortcuts: everyone has handled household acid, so bench discipline decays fastest here
cons.example: a quick pickle dip done without goggles because it is only a few seconds and the piece is small

cons.claim: Corrosive controls can be mistaken for cyanide controls, encouraging a shop to believe one set of habits covers both
cons.example: an acid-zone spill kit is assumed to serve the whole room, which is exactly the crossing the segregation line forbids

failure_modes: adding water to concentrated acid and producing a violent exotherm and spray
skipping eye protection for short tasks, which is when most splashes happen
storing an acid above eye level or above an incompatible neighbour
leaving fuming tanks uncovered when idle so the whole room becomes a corrosive environment
acceptance_tests: the dilution order rule is written at the point of use wherever concentrated acid is diluted
eye and face protection is present and worn for every acid or hot-alkali task, including short ones
idle fuming tanks are covered, and corrosion damage to extraction, cabinets and electrical fittings is inspected on a stated cadence
revisit_triggers: a new acid or alkaline product, or a change in concentration held
visible corrosion appearing on safety-critical equipment
an eye or skin injury or near miss involving a corrosive
tank layout changes that put a corrosive nearer a walkway or a door

base.update_signal: a corrosive injury or near miss occurs, a new acid or alkali is introduced, or corrosion is found on a safety-critical component

nodes.definition: Handle the nickel used in strikes and barrier underplates as the chronic hazard it is rather than the routine bath it feels like: nickel salts carry a skin-sensitiser classification and their inhalable forms carry a carcinogen classification class, which is why two specific habits are forbidden on a plating bench — air agitation of a nickel bath, which turns the tank into a mist generator, and dry mechanical work on nickel-bearing surfaces, which makes respirable dust. Sensitisation is the outcome that ends careers quietly: once a jeweller is sensitised, the reaction persists for life and can be triggered by the metal in their own work. The discipline is glove and mist control every day rather than heroics on bad days, and the routing rule is absolute: a rash, a cough or a suspected sensitisation goes to occupational health or a physician, and never to a shop opinion.

included: sensitiser and inhalable-carcinogen hazard classes for nickel chemistry as handled in the shop
the no-air-agitation and no-dry-dust rules as exposure controls
glove and hygiene discipline against cumulative skin contact
routing personal symptoms to professional care
excluded: nickel-release limits for finished skin-contact jewellery and the compliance testing behind them, which is the marking knowledge base
nickel bath performance, stress and brightener chemistry, which belongs to the bath chemistry specialist
diagnosing, grading or treating an allergy, which is medical practice

pros.claim: Naming sensitisation as permanent changes how a jeweller values a box of gloves
pros.example: gloves are changed when contaminated rather than worn all session, because the exposure that matters is cumulative and unspectacular

pros.claim: Two concrete prohibitions carry most of the inhalation risk reduction and are easy to audit
pros.example: air agitation is replaced by cathode-rod or mechanical movement and no dry buffing of nickel-plated work happens in the wet room

cons.claim: The harm is invisible and delayed, so the control decays without an incident to justify it
cons.example: a shop reintroduces an air pump for better agitation because nothing bad appeared to happen the first week

cons.claim: Alternatives to nickel underplating carry their own cost, complexity and proprietary dependence, so the exposure cannot simply be designed away
cons.example: moving to a nickel-free stack for skin-contact work means buying a proprietary system and running it per its own sheet

failure_modes: air-sparging a nickel bath for agitation and creating a respirable mist
dry grinding or buffing nickel-bearing surfaces in the same room as open tanks
treating a persistent hand rash as an irritation to work through
reusing contaminated gloves and spreading nickel to tools, phone and face
acceptance_tests: no air agitation is in use on any nickel bath and no dry nickel-dust operation happens in the plating room
the shop can show a glove-change and hand-hygiene practice tied to nickel tasks rather than to the end of the day
any reported skin or respiratory symptom has a documented referral to professional care rather than a shop remedy
revisit_triggers: a worker reports dermatitis, itching or respiratory symptoms
agitation, filtration or finishing methods change around nickel baths
a nickel-free stack is introduced for skin-contact work
a supplier revises the classification of a nickel product in use

base.update_signal: a worker reports a skin or respiratory symptom, an agitation or finishing method changes near nickel chemistry, or a product classification is revised

nodes.definition: Account for the hazards that have nothing to do with toxicity and everything to do with a wet room full of heat and current: gold and cleaning baths that run hot per their own technical data sheet and burn on contact; immersion heaters that dry-fire, crack a tank or ignite a bench when the solution level drops through evaporation; rectifiers, leads and heater cords living centimetres from splashed solution and wet hands; hydrogen and oxygen evolved at the electrodes during electrocleaning and striking, which accumulate under lids, foam blankets and enclosures; and the steam and drips that come off hot work as it is withdrawn. Heat is also the link between this class and the inhalation classes, because a hotter bath evaporates and mists more, so thermal control and breathing-zone control are two views of one problem.

included: hot-solution burn and steam hazards during transfer and withdrawal
heater dry-fire and level-loss failure modes
electrical safety around wet benches and rectifiers
evolved hydrogen and oxygen accumulating under covers
heat as a driver of evaporation, mist and vapour load
excluded: choosing the operating temperature or current density, which belongs to the bath chemistry and process execution specialists
deposit quality consequences of temperature drift
electrical installation work itself, which is a qualified trade

pros.claim: Treating heat and current as a named hazard class catches the failures that quietly precede a fire or a shock in a small shop
pros.example: a low-level cut-out and a routine level check are added after a heater is found running in a bath that had evaporated over a long weekend

pros.claim: Recognising gas accumulation under covers reconciles the lid-on habit with the gas-evolution risk instead of leaving the two rules in conflict
pros.example: lids are used on idle tanks but never on a tank that is under current, and enclosures are vented rather than sealed

cons.claim: Thermal and electrical hazards feel mundane next to a fatal gas, so they lose attention exactly where injuries are frequent
cons.example: the shop rehearses its gas-alarm response but has never thought about who switches off the rectifier during a spill

cons.claim: Some mitigations trade against process quality and cost, which invites informal compromises
cons.example: an operator lowers the extraction to stop a hot bath cooling and losing evaporation, quietly reversing the control hierarchy

failure_modes: an immersion heater exposed above a fallen solution level
a rectifier, lead or extension socket sitting where solution can reach it
sealing an energised tank under a tight cover and accumulating evolved gas
carrying hot work over a walkway or over an incompatible tank
acceptance_tests: heaters have a level or dry-fire safeguard, and the level check is part of the pre-run gate
electrical equipment is mounted or shielded so that a credible splash or overflow cannot reach it, and the emergency stop is reachable without crossing the spill
no energised tank is operated under a sealed cover
revisit_triggers: a heater, rectifier or tank is added, moved or replaced
evaporation losses change after a ventilation or lid change
a burn, shock or scorch near miss is logged
the room layout changes the route hot work travels

base.update_signal: equipment is added, moved or replaced, evaporation behaviour changes, or a thermal or electrical near miss is logged

nodes.definition: Hold the one line on a plating bench that has no exception, no shortcut and no experienced-operator variant: cyanide-bearing solutions and acids are never mixed, never stored together, never allowed to share a drain, and never allowed to share a spill path, a pump, a scoop, a brush, a rinse vessel, a drip tray or a splash zone. Because a lapse here produces a rapidly fatal gas rather than a spoiled batch, segregation is built as a physical property of the premises rather than as a behaviour people maintain: distinct zones separated by distance or a barrier, separate containment, separate or absent drainage, dedicated and visibly marked equipment that never crosses, and a one-way route for work so a wet acid rack never travels over or past a cyanide tank. Every change to the room — a new bench, a borrowed pump, a rearranged shelf, a plumber's visit — is re-checked against this line before the next run.

included: zoning by distance or physical barrier
dedicated, marked equipment and protective gear per zone
one-way work routing that never carries acid-wet work over cyanide vessels
re-verification of the line after any change to the room
the rule that this applies to rinses and drag-out, not only to baths
excluded: what happens to the two segregated streams once they are waste, which is the waste knowledge base
the plating sequence and transfer timing itself, which belongs to process execution
any claim that a careful procedure, a rule about order of work, or an experienced operator can substitute for physical separation

pros.claim: Building the line into the room means it survives fatigue, distraction and the person who was not there when the rule was explained
pros.example: an apprentice cannot rinse an acid-wet rack in the cyanide drag-out because the two zones are in different parts of the room with their own dedicated vessels and no shared sink

pros.claim: A physical line is auditable in seconds by an inspector, an insurer or a visiting jeweller, which keeps it honest
pros.example: the shop can point to the barrier, the two colour-coded tool sets and the capped drain rather than describing an intention

cons.claim: Full physical segregation consumes floor space and duplicate equipment that a small bench feels acutely
cons.example: two spill kits, two sets of gauntlets, two pumps and two waste containers in a room that barely fits one line

cons.claim: Duplication creates its own failure mode when equipment looks similar, so marking and discipline still carry load
cons.example: two identical pumps bought at the same time end up used interchangeably unless one is permanently marked and stored in its zone

failure_modes: a shared sink, floor drain or wash-down hose serving both zones
a tool, pump, glove, tray or bucket used in both zones because it was the one at hand
acid stored on a shelf above or beside cyanide stock because the corrosive cabinet was full
a room change made without re-checking the line, particularly plumbing or shelving work done by someone else
acceptance_tests: a visitor can be shown the acid zone, the cyanide zone and the physical thing that separates them, and the shop can state where a spill in each zone would end up
no vessel, tool, pump, glove, tray or protective item is used in both zones, and each is marked to its zone
the work route is walked and no path carries acid-wet work over or beside a cyanide vessel
a re-check of the line is recorded after every change to the room's layout, plumbing or equipment
revisit_triggers: any layout, plumbing, shelving or equipment change, including work done by a landlord or contractor
a new chemistry that introduces acid or cyanide where there was none
a near miss involving a crossed tool, vessel or route
a second person starts working in the room

base.update_signal: the room, its plumbing or its equipment changes, or an audit finds a shared item or path between the two zones

nodes.definition: Answer for every vessel in the room the question nobody asks until it is too late — if this fell over right now, where would the contents go — and then engineer the answer rather than hope for it: secondary containment trays or bunds sized to the largest credible container failure in each zone, thresholds or kerbs that stop liquid travelling between zones, absorbent barriers stored where the liquid would reach them, tanks sited away from doorways and traffic, and a deliberate decision about floor drains, which in a plating room are usually capped or removed because a drain is a route by which two segregated streams meet out of sight. This is the physical half of the segregation line and the first thing an insurer, an inspector or a landlord will look at, because it is the only part of a safety case that cannot be improvised on the morning of a visit.

included: containment volume logic per zone
drain capping, isolation and the no-shared-drain rule
a walked spill-path map for every vessel
siting decisions relative to doors, walkways and services
floor and threshold construction as a containment element
excluded: treating, neutralising or discharging captured liquid, which is the waste knowledge base and is never done to a drain here
deciding whether any treated stream may lawfully be discharged, which is a jurisdiction and waste question
plumbing work itself, which is a qualified trade

pros.claim: Sizing containment to the largest credible failure converts a catastrophic spill into a contained mess
pros.example: a cracked twenty-litre tank empties into its bund instead of running under the bench toward the acid zone

pros.claim: Capping the floor drain removes the invisible path by which segregation is most often defeated
pros.example: a rinse-water spill can no longer reach the same pipe the pickle bench drains to, which is the pathway that makes gas out of sight of everyone

cons.claim: Containment takes floor area, raises working height and makes wash-down slower and more manual
cons.example: bunded trays under every tank turn a quick mop-out into a pump-and-absorb job

cons.claim: Containment holds the spill but creates a new decision about the captured liquid that the shop must be ready to hand to a licensed route
cons.example: a bund full of mixed rinse and bath solution is now a waste characterization question rather than a cleaning question

failure_modes: containment sized to a typical spill rather than to the largest vessel present
an uncapped or forgotten floor drain, especially one under a bench or behind equipment
bunds used as storage shelves so their capacity is consumed by boxes
a spill path that crosses a doorway, so the response has to happen in the escape route
acceptance_tests: every vessel has a documented answer to where its contents would go, and each zone's worst credible spill is contained inside that zone
no drain is shared between the acid and cyanide zones, and any drain in the wet area is capped or isolated with that fact recorded
containment capacity is clear of stored items at the start of every run
revisit_triggers: a new or larger vessel is introduced
plumbing, flooring or drainage work is done by anyone, including the landlord
a spill occurs and travels further than the map predicted
the room is rearranged or a bench is added

base.update_signal: a vessel, bench, drain or floor changes, or a real spill travels differently from the mapped path

nodes.definition: Store by class rather than by convenience: cyanide salts and concentrates locked, dry, ventilated and physically remote from every acid and oxidiser and from any water route; acids in a dedicated corrosive cabinet with a compatible liner; alkalis separate from acids; oxidisers separate from everything; nothing stored above head height or above an incompatible neighbour; every container on secondary containment; and stock quantities deliberately kept small, because the cheapest control available to a small shop is not holding the material in the first place. Security is part of storage wherever cyanide is present — controlled access, a named holder, and a stock ledger that would reveal a loss — and the quantity bands, cabinet requirements and licensing conditions attached to all of this are read from the jurisdiction register with a date, never assumed from another country's practice.

included: incompatibility-based storage classes and physical separation
access control, named holder and stock ledger for cyanide-bearing stock
height, containment and quantity-minimisation rules
ordering discipline capped by storage capacity
excluded: asserting the quantity threshold at which a licence, cabinet or notification becomes required in any jurisdiction
waste storage duration and manifesting once material is declared waste, which is the waste knowledge base
security advice beyond the safety-driven access-control class

pros.claim: Class-based storage makes an incompatible neighbour visible at a glance instead of discoverable by accident
pros.example: the acid cabinet is on the opposite wall from the locked cyanide store, so a hurried put-away has nowhere wrong to go

pros.claim: Capping order size at cabinet capacity turns purchasing into a safety control
pros.example: the shop buys acid in quantities the corrosive cabinet can hold rather than taking the bulk discount that would force floor storage

cons.claim: Small, frequent purchases cost more per unit and more in delivery, which pushes a cost-pressed shop toward bulk
cons.example: buying five one-litre bottles over a year costs noticeably more than one five-litre container that would not fit the cabinet

cons.claim: Locked storage adds friction to legitimate work and is the control most often defeated by leaving the key in the lock
cons.example: the cyanide store is unlocked at the start of the day and stays open until closing because opening it repeatedly is tedious

failure_modes: acid stacked in or beside the cyanide store because the corrosive cabinet is full
containers stored above head height where a fall lands on a person
the locked store left open through the working day
no stock ledger, so a missing container is never noticed
acceptance_tests: incompatible classes are physically separated and each store's contents match the chemical register
cyanide-bearing stock is under controlled access with a named holder and a ledger that would reveal a discrepancy
no container is stored above head height or above an incompatible neighbour, and every container sits on containment
the maximum order size for each class is written and derived from storage capacity
revisit_triggers: a delivery that would exceed cabinet or store capacity
a change in the jurisdiction register affecting quantity or security conditions
a new class of chemical entering the shop
a ledger discrepancy or a missing container

base.update_signal: storage capacity, held quantities or the jurisdiction's storage and security conditions change, or a ledger discrepancy appears

nodes.definition: Give every vessel in the room an identity and never let one lose it: supplier labels kept intact and legible, every decant labelled at the moment of pouring with contents, hazard class, concentration where known and date, working tanks labelled including the ones that look like water — the rinse cascade and the static drag-out that holds bath solution by design — and an absolute ban on food or drink containers as chemical vessels, because the day someone drinks from a fizzy-drink bottle of pickle is a day that has happened in real workshops. The failure this discipline exists to prevent is the unlabelled beaker: the single object that turns a routine tidy-up into an acid-into-cyanide event because the person holding it does not know what it is and reasonably assumes it is spent rinse water.

included: supplier label integrity and replacement when damaged
decant labelling at the moment of transfer
labelling of tanks, rinses and drag-out vessels
the food-container prohibition
the handling rule for a vessel whose identity is lost
excluded: waste container labelling and manifest coding once material is declared waste, which is the waste knowledge base
product marking and hallmarking of the finished jewellery, which is the marking knowledge base
designing a compliant label format, which follows the supplier sheet and local rules

pros.claim: Labelling at the moment of decanting is the cheapest control in the shop and removes the most dangerous ambiguity
pros.example: a beaker of dilute acid drawn off for a quick dip carries its identity for the twenty minutes it sits on the bench

pros.claim: Labelling the invisible vessels corrects the mental model that only the bath is hazardous
pros.example: the drag-out bucket is marked as cyanide-bearing solution, so nobody empties it into the pickle-side sink while cleaning up

cons.claim: Labels degrade in exactly the environment that most needs them, so the discipline is maintenance rather than a one-off
cons.example: acid fume and splash render a printed tank label unreadable within months and it has to be reprinted and protected

cons.claim: Rigorous labelling slows small ad-hoc tasks and is the first step skipped under time pressure
cons.example: a two-minute decant done unlabelled because the operator intends to use it immediately, and then the phone rings

failure_modes: an unlabelled vessel left on a bench between zones
a food or drink container used for a chemical
a supplier label obscured, corroded or torn off with no replacement
a decant labelled with only a name, so concentration and date are unknown when it matters
acceptance_tests: no unlabelled vessel exists in the room at the end of any work session, verified by a walk-round
every tank, rinse and drag-out vessel carries a label naming its contents and hazard class
no food or drink container holds any chemical anywhere in the premises
the shop has a written rule that a vessel of unknown identity is isolated in containment and routed to licensed disposal rather than tested, poured or mixed
revisit_triggers: an unlabelled or unidentifiable vessel is found
labels are found degraded or unreadable during a walk-round
a new decanting task or a new product enters routine use
a new person starts work and the labelling convention has to be legible to them

base.update_signal: an unlabelled vessel is found, a new decanting routine begins, or labels are found degraded during a walk-round

nodes.definition: Treat extraction as an obligation class with a specific shape: capture at the source, at the tank, before mist and vapour reach the operator's breathing zone — a slot or lip extract, a partial enclosure, a hood over the tank — rather than a room fan, an open window or a domestic extractor that merely stirs and redistributes contaminated air. The obligation extends past installation into verification, because extraction degrades invisibly as ducts load, filters clog, fans slip and someone stores a box against the intake: a tell-tale, a smoke check or an airflow indicator on a stated interval is what converts a fan into a control. Lids on idle tanks reduce the emission at source and make the extraction's job possible. The enforceable requirement and its test interval come from the local workplace authority, and the honest conclusion is stated plainly: a room that cannot host source capture cannot host these chemistries, whatever the equipment cost.

included: source capture versus room dilution as a design distinction
verification routine and its evidence
lids and enclosure as emission reduction at source
discharge siting away from intakes, doors and neighbours
the no-capture-no-chemistry conclusion
excluded: specifying capture velocities, duct sizes or air-change figures, which are engineering and jurisdiction questions to verify locally
air-permit and emission-limit compliance for what is discharged, which is the waste and environmental knowledge base
scrubber selection and design, which is a supplier and engineering matter

pros.claim: Capture at the tank removes the contaminant before the room ever sees it, which is the only control that works while people are busy
pros.example: a lip extract along the pickle and gold tanks keeps fume out of the breathing zone during the transfer that no protective equipment covers well

pros.claim: A scheduled verification turns an invisible control into an observable one, catching the slow failures
pros.example: a monthly tell-tale check finds capture has dropped since a storage box was pushed against the duct intake

cons.claim: Extraction removes heat and moisture from hot baths, so it costs energy, drives evaporation and speeds carbonate-forming exchange with room air
cons.example: a hot gold bath under strong capture needs more frequent make-up and more attentive analysis than the same bath in an unextracted room

cons.claim: A compliant installation for a small shop is expensive and often needs landlord permission for ducting through the building fabric
cons.example: the run to an external discharge point crosses a shared wall and requires the landlord's agreement before anything can be installed

failure_modes: a room fan or open window used as if it were source capture
storage, work or a hung rack blocking the capture slot
discharge sited beside an air intake, an opening window or a neighbour's doorway
no verification routine, so a degraded system is trusted for years
acceptance_tests: capture is demonstrated at the tank with a smoke or tell-tale check on the shop's stated interval and the result recorded
the discharge point is sited away from intakes, openings and occupied neighbouring space, and that siting is documented
idle tanks are covered and the capture slot is clear at the start of every run
the shop can state which authority sets the requirement it is verifying against and when it last confirmed it
revisit_triggers: a tank is added, moved, enlarged or run hotter
a verification check shows reduced capture
building work, a new neighbour or a changed discharge environment
a new chemistry with a different emission behaviour is introduced

base.update_signal: a verification check shows reduced capture, the tank layout or thermal load changes, or the local authority restates the ventilation requirement

nodes.definition: Where free-cyanide chemistry is run, published industrial-hygiene practice treats hydrogen-cyanide detection with an audible alarm as part of the room, not as an optional upgrade, and the shop's real work is in the maintenance and the response rule rather than the purchase. Maintenance means a functional bump test on a stated interval, a calibration record, a sensor end-of-life date tracked because electrochemical sensors expire whether or not they are used, placement where gas would actually reach the sensor, and an alarm loud enough to be heard over an ultrasonic bath and a compressor. The response rule is one sentence and is rehearsed rather than reasoned about in the moment: an alarm means leave and ventilate, never investigate, and nobody re-enters for equipment or work. A detector nobody has bump-tested provides reassurance rather than protection, which is worse than no detector because it changes behaviour without changing risk.

included: detection as an obligation class for free-cyanide operations
bump test, calibration and sensor end-of-life discipline
placement and audibility
the leave-and-ventilate response rule and the no-re-entry rule
excluded: specifying alarm set points or exposure limits, which are jurisdiction and manufacturer values to verify
selecting a particular instrument or brand
interpreting a reading as a health assessment of an individual, which is medical territory

pros.claim: A working alarm converts an invisible, odour-unreliable hazard into a signal a person can act on
pros.example: a detector alarms during a bath addition and the room is cleared before anyone recognises symptoms

pros.claim: A rehearsed one-sentence response removes the decision from the moment when judgement is least reliable
pros.example: the operator leaves at the alarm rather than pausing to shut down the rectifier and save the work in the tank

cons.claim: Detection creates a false-security failure mode: an unmaintained instrument silently stops protecting while everyone behaves as if it does
cons.example: a sensor two years past its life still shows a green light and has never been challenged with test gas

cons.claim: Recurring calibration and sensor replacement is an ongoing cost and an administrative burden that small shops let lapse first
cons.example: the annual calibration is deferred because the job schedule is full, and the deferral becomes permanent

failure_modes: a detector never bump-tested since installation
a sensor past its end-of-life date still trusted
the alarm inaudible over the equipment actually running during work
someone investigating the alarm instead of leaving, especially to protect gold-bearing work
acceptance_tests: a bump test is recorded on the stated interval, with calibration and sensor end-of-life dates tracked and in date
the alarm is demonstrably audible at the working position with the noisiest normal equipment running
the leave-and-ventilate response has been rehearsed with everyone who works in or shares the premises
an out-of-date or failed detector stops free-cyanide work at the readiness gate
revisit_triggers: a bump test fails, a calibration lapses, or a sensor approaches end of life
an alarm event of any kind, including one judged to be false
layout, ventilation or equipment noise changes
free-cyanide chemistry is introduced, expanded or removed

base.update_signal: a bump test or calibration result changes, a sensor reaches end of life, or an alarm event occurs and is investigated

nodes.definition: Keep every free-cyanide solution, and every rinse and drag-out vessel that has touched one, comfortably above its alkaline floor, and treat that pH as a safety measurement with its own log rather than as one more process reading: published plating chemistry places the practical floor for free-cyanide solutions around pH 10.5 and the specific product's technical data sheet governs the working window it must actually sit in. The discipline has three parts. Measure on a schedule and after any addition or top-up, including after a bath has stood idle. Correct upward only, with the alkali the technical data sheet names, and never bring any acid near the bath or its rinses for any reason, including cleaning. Understand that the drift is one-way and predictable, because absorbed carbon dioxide from room air and drag-in from earlier tanks push pH down over time, so a bath left standing over a long weekend is the classic case that must be checked before the lid is lifted rather than after.

included: pH as a life-safety measurement with its own record
upward-only correction with the alkali named by the technical data sheet
the one-way carbon-dioxide and drag-in drift mechanism
inclusion of rinses and drag-out vessels in the regime
the escalation when a reading is below the floor
excluded: bath performance tuning such as gold concentration, current density, brightener additions and deposit quality, which belong to the bath chemistry and process execution specialists
any acid-side adjustment of any kind
treatment or destruction chemistry for spent solutions, which is the waste knowledge base

pros.claim: Logging pH as a safety parameter makes the drift visible before it reaches the floor rather than after
pros.example: a slow weekly decline in a standing bath is spotted in the log and corrected long before any gas evolution is credible

pros.claim: An upward-only correction rule removes the single most catastrophic bench mistake from the space of possible actions
pros.example: nobody reaches for an acid to bring a bath back into a colour or performance window, because the rule admits no acid near the tank

cons.claim: Measurement itself needs maintained equipment and technique, so an unmaintained meter can manufacture false confidence
cons.example: an uncalibrated pH meter with a dried electrode reads high and the shop believes a drifting bath is fine

cons.claim: Safety monitoring adds readings and record-keeping to every session, including sessions where no plating is done
cons.example: a bath standing unused still has to be checked and logged, which feels like paperwork about nothing until the one time it is not

failure_modes: checking pH only when plating quality suffers rather than on a schedule
using an uncalibrated or dried-out meter and trusting the number
correcting with an unspecified alkali instead of the one the technical data sheet names
opening or agitating a bath that has stood idle before checking it
acceptance_tests: a pH log exists for every cyanide-bearing vessel with readings on the stated schedule and after every addition
the correction alkali named by the technical data sheet is the only pH-adjusting material present in the cyanide zone
the meter or method has a calibration record and a stated check routine
a written escalation states what happens if a reading is below the floor: do not open or agitate, ventilate, and involve an authorized trained person with detection running
revisit_triggers: any reading approaching or below the floor
a bath left standing longer than usual, or returning from a shutdown
a technical data sheet revision that changes the working window
a change in room ventilation or agitation that alters carbon-dioxide exchange

base.update_signal: a reading approaches the floor, the technical data sheet revises the window, or the measurement method's calibration record lapses

nodes.definition: Derive protective equipment per task from the product's safety data sheet rather than from habit or from what is in the drawer: glove material and thickness chosen against the specific chemical and its breakthrough behaviour, since a thin examination glove is a hygiene item and not a chemical gauntlet; a face shield over eye protection wherever splash, hot solution or a lift out of a tank is involved; a chemical apron and closed footwear for tank work; and a doffing routine that keeps contamination on the outside of the equipment, meaning gloves come off before a phone, a door handle, a face or a coffee. The care half matters as much as the selection: inspection before use, replacement on contamination rather than at the end of the week, storage that keeps the two zones' equipment separate, and the standing rule that a task requiring protection the shop does not currently own does not run today. Protective equipment is the last line of defence and is never the answer to a problem that extraction or segregation should have solved.

included: sheet-derived selection per task and per chemical
inspection, replacement and contamination-aware doffing
zone-separated storage of protective equipment
the no-equipment-no-job rule
the hierarchy position of protection as the last line
excluded: respiratory protective equipment programmes involving fit testing and medical clearance, which require a qualified provider and are named as an escalation rather than run here
substituting protection for source capture or segregation
selecting equipment for waste handling and transport tasks, which is the waste knowledge base

pros.claim: Sheet-derived selection replaces a debate with a lookup and catches the mismatches habit produces
pros.example: a glove that resists an acid pickle is found to be the wrong choice for a solvent-bearing stripper, and the correct material is bought before the task runs

pros.claim: A doffing routine stops the contamination that protective equipment quietly spreads around the shop
pros.example: gloves come off before touching the phone, so cyanide-bearing film does not travel to a face later in the day

cons.claim: Correct heavy protection reduces dexterity and vision, which introduces its own hazards during delicate jewellery handling
cons.example: gauntlets and a face shield make it harder to place a small ring on a rack over a hot tank, raising the chance of a drop and a splash

cons.claim: Equipment is a consumable whose replacement cost recurs and whose degradation is easy to ignore
cons.example: gauntlets stiffen and craze after months of pickle exposure and are still used because they have no visible hole

failure_modes: thin examination gloves used for tank work because they are what is on the bench
eye protection without a face shield for a lift out of a hot tank
protective equipment carried between zones, defeating the segregation line
damaged or expired equipment kept in service because it looks intact
acceptance_tests: each routine task names its protective equipment and the sheet section that equipment was derived from
gloves and gauntlets are inspected before use and replaced on contamination or degradation, with the rule written
each zone's protective equipment is stored in that zone and never crosses
the shop can point to at least one task it has deferred for missing protective equipment
revisit_triggers: a new chemical or a reformulated product
a sheet revision changing protection guidance
any splash, permeation or skin-contact incident
a new task or handling method that changes the exposure

base.update_signal: a sheet revision changes protection guidance, a new chemical or task appears, or a permeation or splash incident is reported

nodes.definition: Decide who is allowed to do what, on evidence rather than on seniority or willingness: formal external hazardous-material and workplace-safety training as the prerequisite for anyone who will handle cyanide chemistry at all, documented in-shop competency sign-off task by task — bath make-up, additions, transfer, rinse and drag-out handling, spill response, shutdown — a named authorization list for who may open, move or decant cyanide-bearing stock, refresher and re-authorization triggers, and an induction for anyone who merely shares the premises, including a landlord, a cleaner or a family member in a home workshop. The rule that this node exists to make schedulable rather than aspirational is the one small shops break most often: free-cyanide work is never done alone, because a second trained person who can raise an alarm is part of the control set, and a jeweller working late by themselves has silently removed a control they were relying on.

included: external formal training as a prerequisite class
per-task competency sign-off and the authorization list
the no-lone-working rule for free-cyanide work, expressed as a scheduling constraint
refresher and re-authorization triggers
induction for anyone sharing the premises
excluded: delivering the training or issuing any certification, which requires a qualified provider
personalised judgements about an individual's fitness, health or capability, which belong to occupational health
employment and disciplinary process, which is a management and legal matter beyond this scope

pros.claim: An authorization list converts a vague sense of who knows what into a checkable fact at the moment work is scheduled
pros.example: the ring order cannot start because the only person on shift is signed off for rinse handling but not for bath make-up

pros.claim: Treating the no-lone-working rule as a rota constraint rather than a poster makes it survive a busy week
pros.example: cyanide tasks are scheduled only on days when a second trained person is present, and late solo sessions are limited to non-cyanide work

cons.claim: A one-person shop cannot satisfy the second-person requirement without changing its business model, which is a hard and unwelcome finding
cons.example: a solo jeweller concludes that free-cyanide work must be outsourced or a partner trained, because there is no third option

cons.claim: Formal training costs money and calendar time and may be hard to source locally for a very small operation
cons.example: the nearest suitable chemical-handling course runs twice a year and requires travel, which delays the shop's start date

failure_modes: the busy-week substitution where an unauthorized person does the make-up because the job was already promised
training treated as a one-off event with no refresher trigger
no induction for people who share the building and would be in the room during an incident
the lone-working rule kept as a written intention while the rota routinely breaks it
acceptance_tests: every person who touches the chemistry has documented external training plus in-shop sign-off for each task they perform
the authorization list names who may open, move or decant cyanide-bearing stock, and is current
the rota shows free-cyanide tasks scheduled only when a second trained person is present
anyone who shares the premises has a recorded induction covering the alarm response and the zones
revisit_triggers: a new person joins, leaves or changes tasks
a new chemistry or task class is introduced
an incident, near miss or drill reveals a competence gap
a refresher interval elapses or a regulator changes the training duty

base.update_signal: headcount or task allocation changes, a refresher interval elapses, or a drill or incident exposes a competence gap

nodes.definition: Convert the safety data sheet, the technical data sheet and the method actually taught in training into short written instructions per task that live at the bench where the task happens, not in a manual in an office: what is worn, what is switched on and verified before a lid comes off, the order of moves, the stop conditions that end the task early, and what the operator does when something is not as expected — which is usually stop, isolate, and call rather than improvise. Change control carries as much weight as the writing: each instruction is dated, has an owner, and is reissued when the product, the room, the equipment or the person changes, because a shop that simply knows its method has no mechanism for noticing that the method drifted. The instruction never invents a setpoint; where a number is needed it points at the technical data sheet or the shop's own logged runs.

included: short task cards at the point of use
pre-task verification steps and explicit stop conditions
dating, ownership and reissue on change
pointing at the technical data sheet rather than restating setpoints
excluded: writing procedures for chemistry the shop is not trained and authorized to run, which is improvisation with extra steps
waste handling and shipping procedures, which belong to the waste knowledge base
customer-facing claim wording, which belongs to the marking knowledge base

pros.claim: A card at the bench is used; a manual in an office is not, and the difference shows up in the first busy week
pros.example: the make-up card hanging beside the cyanide zone is read before each addition, including by the person who has done it fifty times

pros.claim: Explicit stop conditions give an operator permission to abandon a task without needing to justify it in the moment
pros.example: the card states that a pH reading below the floor ends the task and starts the escalation, so nobody has to make that call under pressure

cons.claim: Written instructions age into fiction if change control is not enforced, and a wrong card is more dangerous than none
cons.example: the card still names a glove and a correction alkali from a product the shop stopped buying a year ago

cons.claim: Over-long procedures are ignored wholesale, so the discipline is compression rather than completeness
cons.example: a six-page procedure for a fifteen-minute task is skimmed once and never opened again

failure_modes: instructions written from memory rather than from the sheet and the trained method
an undated card with no owner, so nobody knows whether it is current
a card that restates a setpoint the technical data sheet has since changed
no stop conditions, leaving the operator to improvise at exactly the wrong moment
acceptance_tests: every routine task has a dated, owned instruction at its point of use
each instruction names its protective equipment, its pre-task verifications and at least one explicit stop condition
instructions are reissued when the product, room, equipment or person changes, with the previous version withdrawn from the bench
no instruction states a setpoint as fact; each points at the technical data sheet or the shop's own logged runs
revisit_triggers: a product, room, equipment or personnel change
a near miss or incident that touched the task
a technical data sheet revision
a drill or observation showing the written method and the practised method have diverged

base.update_signal: a product, room or equipment change, a sheet revision, or an observed divergence between the written and the practised method

nodes.definition: Provide and prove the first thirty seconds of a corrosive or hot-solution injury: an eyewash within immediate, unobstructed reach of the tanks, of a type that delivers a long hands-free flush to both eyes rather than a squeeze bottle that empties in seconds, plus a drench facility where corrosives or hot alkali are handled in quantity, flushed and recorded on a schedule so the first litre is not stagnant, kept from freezing or overheating, and never allowed to become a shelf, a coat hook or the place the boxes go.
