Readiness here is a physical property that must be tested by walking it, ideally with eyes closed and a guide, because an injured person will be doing exactly that; if the route takes longer than seconds or requires opening a door and finding a light switch, the provision is decorative. The flush is first aid that buys time before professional care, and never a reason to skip the call.

included: provision type, siting and unobstructed reach
scheduled flushing and its record
the walked reachability test
the rule that flushing never replaces the emergency call
excluded: clinical guidance on flush duration or after-care for a specific injury, which is medical and comes from emergency services and the safety data sheet
specifying a standard-compliant fixture, which is a jurisdiction and equipment question
treatment decisions of any kind

pros.claim: A hands-free long flush within seconds is the single intervention that most changes the outcome of a corrosive eye splash
pros.example: an operator splashed while lifting work from a hot alkaline cleaner reaches the station without help and flushes while a second person calls

pros.claim: The walked reachability test finds the obstruction nobody notices, because the route is normally walked with open eyes and free hands
pros.example: the test shows a rolling stool and a stack of boxes now sit between the tanks and the station

cons.claim: Plumbed provision needs water, drainage and freeze protection that a small or converted workshop may not have
cons.example: an unheated garage bench cannot host a plumbed station, which forces a different and less capable arrangement that must be honestly acknowledged

cons.claim: Scheduled flushing is a recurring chore with no visible benefit, so it is the first record to lapse
cons.example: the weekly flush log has three months of blanks and the first litre runs discoloured when finally tested

failure_modes: a small squeeze bottle treated as sufficient provision for a two-eye splash
the route obstructed by stools, boxes, racks or a closed door
stagnant water in an unflushed line delivered into an injured eye
flushing treated as the whole response so no call is made
acceptance_tests: the station is reachable from every tank position in seconds with eyes closed and hands occupied, verified by a walked test with a guide
a flush record exists on the stated schedule and the water runs clear
the route and the station area are clear at the start of every run
the written response pairs flushing with an emergency call rather than treating it as the endpoint
revisit_triggers: the room is rearranged or a tank position moves
a flush check finds discoloured water or reduced flow
a splash incident or near miss
seasonal conditions threaten freezing or overheating of the supply

base.update_signal: a walked reachability test or flush check fails, the room is rearranged, or a splash incident is logged

nodes.definition: Be ready for the spill in the only way that works, which is two separate kits that never meet: one for the acid zone and one for the cyanide zone, each sized to the largest credible spill in that zone, each holding the absorbent and containment materials appropriate to its own class and holding nothing that would react with the other zone's chemistry — an acid neutraliser must never be carried into the cyanide zone, and the temptation to keep one universal kit for tidiness is the segregation line failing in a cardboard box. Alongside the materials sits a written size-decision rule that removes judgement from the moment: what the shop cleans up itself, what it contains and then calls about, and what it simply evacuates from. In the cyanide zone the first branch is evacuation and ventilation rather than cleanup, and the captured material becomes a regulated-waste question for the waste specialist rather than a mopping question. Readiness is maintained by inventory checks and by restocking immediately after any use, because a kit used once and not refilled is an empty box with a reassuring label.

included: one kit per zone, never shared, never crossed
kit sizing against the largest credible spill in the zone
the written clean-up versus contain versus evacuate decision rule
restocking and inventory discipline
handover of captured material to the regulated-waste route
excluded: treating, neutralising or disposing of the captured material, which is the waste knowledge base
any improvised neutralisation of a cyanide-bearing spill, which is never done in the shop
emergency service tactics, which belong to responders

pros.claim: Zone-dedicated kits make the correct material the only material within reach, which is what actually decides behaviour in a spill
pros.example: the cyanide-zone kit contains absorbent and containment only, so there is no acid neutraliser anywhere near the solution that would react with it

pros.claim: A written size rule prevents the most common bad outcome, which is a lone operator trying to clean up something they should have walked away from
pros.example: a broken twenty-litre container triggers evacuate-and-call while a drip under a rack is wiped up under the routine rule

cons.claim: Duplicate kits cost money and space and are the first purchase deferred in a small shop
cons.example: a second full kit for the acid zone is postponed and the cyanide-zone kit quietly becomes the shop's only one

cons.claim: Kits decay silently through partial use, evaporation and borrowed items
cons.example: the absorbent has been raided for routine drips and the kit is half empty when it is finally needed

failure_modes: one universal kit serving both zones
an acid neutraliser stored in or carried into the cyanide zone
a kit used and not restocked
an operator attempting a cleanup that the size rule says should have been an evacuation
acceptance_tests: each zone holds its own kit, marked to that zone, containing nothing incompatible with that zone's chemistry
kit contents are inventoried on the stated cadence and restocked immediately after any use
the clean-up versus contain versus evacuate rule is written, posted in the zone, and rehearsed
the written rule routes captured spill material to the regulated-waste path rather than to any drain
revisit_triggers: any spill, however small, including one cleaned up routinely
a change in the largest container size held in a zone
a kit inventory check that finds items missing or expired
a new chemistry class whose spill behaviour differs from what the kit was built for

base.update_signal: a spill occurs, the largest container size in a zone changes, or an inventory check finds the kit incomplete

nodes.definition: Write the plan for a person rather than for a floor, and rehearse it: remove from exposure, flush or decontaminate as the safety data sheet directs, call emergency services immediately and say the actual chemical name — the word cyanide changes what arrives and how fast — and hand or send the sheet with the patient so responders and clinicians are working from the product rather than from a description. Anyone exposed goes for professional assessment even when they feel well, because several of these classes present with delay. Where a cyanide antidote provision is expected for a site, it is arranged, stored and governed with local medical guidance and the local emergency service and is never self-prescribed, self-administered or improvised by the shop. Everything personal routes outward: a rash after a nickel run, a cough, a suspected sensitisation, a fitness-to-work question and any after-care decision go to occupational health or a physician. The shop's job in an exposure is accurate information, speed, and honesty about what was in the tank; it is never diagnosis, dosing or reassurance.

included: the remove, decontaminate, call and hand-over-the-sheet sequence
naming the chemical explicitly to responders
the go-anyway rule for people who feel fine
antidote provision as a locally-governed arrangement class
routing all symptoms and after-care to professional providers
excluded: any medical advice, dose, treatment or triage instruction
deciding whether a person is fit to return to work
diagnosing a nickel allergy or any other condition
assuming an antidote exists on site or that anyone in the shop may administer one

pros.claim: Naming the chemical on the call changes the response that is dispatched and the treatment considered
pros.example: the caller says the word cyanide and the product name rather than describing a yellow solution, and the sheet goes with the patient

pros.claim: A go-anyway rule removes the most dangerous judgement call from a shaken person at the bench
pros.example: an operator who inhaled briefly and feels fine is assessed rather than sent back to work on their own assurance

cons.claim: The plan is only as good as the information handover, which fails when sheets are not at hand or the room is unlabelled
cons.example: responders arrive to find no register, no sheets and nobody able to say what is in the three unlabelled buckets

cons.claim: Antidote provision is jurisdiction-specific, expensive and medically governed, so a shop cannot resolve it internally and may be tempted to skip the question
cons.example: the shop postpones asking the local emergency service what it expects on site because the answer is inconvenient

failure_modes: describing symptoms to a call handler instead of naming the chemical
deciding on the spot that an exposure was too minor to report or assess
no sheet accompanying the patient, leaving clinicians to guess
anyone in the shop attempting a medical intervention beyond first aid they are trained and authorised to give
acceptance_tests: a written exposure plan exists per hazard class, naming the immediate actions, who calls, what is said and what is handed over
the sheets and the chemical register are reachable at the exit so they leave with the patient or meet the responders
the plan has been rehearsed with everyone on site, including people who do not plate
any antidote or special provision question has been put to local medical guidance and the answer recorded with its date
revisit_triggers: any exposure, however minor, or any symptom report
a change in chemistry, supplier or hazard classification
a change in local emergency service arrangements or medical guidance
a drill showing the handover information could not be produced quickly

base.update_signal: an exposure or symptom is reported, the chemistry or its classification changes, or local emergency and medical arrangements are restated

nodes.definition: Make the plan visible and rehearsed rather than filed: hazard and zone signage at the door and at each zone stating what is inside, what to do if the alarm sounds and who to call; an emergency card by the phone carrying the shop's own address, because people forget it under stress; the safety data sheet location marked; and short, scheduled drills — alarm response, spill decision, eyewash route, exposure call — run with whoever is actually on shift, including the people who share the building and do not plate. Where the jurisdiction supports it, pre-notifying the local fire service that cyanide chemistry is present is part of the program, so the crew that arrives already knows what the building holds. The drill is also the cheapest audit the shop will ever run: it is what finds the blocked eyewash, the flat alarm battery, the kit nobody restocked and the person who would have gone back in for the work.

included: door and zone signage content
the emergency card with address and contacts
scheduled drills covering alarm, spill, flush and call
inclusion of non-plating occupants of the premises
responder pre-notification where the jurisdiction supports it
excluded: specifying a legally-compliant sign format or wording, which is a jurisdiction question to verify
customer-facing or marketing signage and claims, which belong to the marking knowledge base
directing emergency service tactics

pros.claim: A drill converts a written plan into a rehearsed reflex and simultaneously audits every readiness item
pros.example: a fifteen-minute alarm drill finds the eyewash blocked by a delivery and the second exit key missing

pros.claim: Pre-notification and door signage give responders the information at the moment they most need it and least can ask for it
pros.example: the crew arriving at a small unit knows before entry that cyanide chemistry is present and where the store is

cons.claim: Drills cost production time and feel theatrical in a one or two-person shop, so they are postponed indefinitely
cons.example: the quarterly drill is skipped three quarters running because the bench is busy and everyone already knows the plan

cons.claim: Signage decays into wallpaper: it stops being read within weeks of installation and can become inaccurate as the room changes
cons.example: the zone sign still lists a chemistry the shop stopped running last year

failure_modes: signage that names hazards but not the response or the contact
drills run only with the owner, so the people who share the building have never practised
an emergency card without the shop's own address
no responder pre-notification in a jurisdiction that expects it
acceptance_tests: door and zone signage states the hazard, the alarm response and the contact, and matches the current chemical register
a drill record shows alarm, spill decision, flush route and exposure call rehearsed on the stated cadence with the people actually present
every drill produces a findings list, and each finding has an owner and a closure date
responder pre-notification has either been made or its status confirmed with the local service and recorded with a date
revisit_triggers: a chemistry, layout or occupancy change that makes signage inaccurate
a drill that reveals a readiness gap
a new person, tenant or neighbour in the premises
a real incident, which replaces the next scheduled drill with a review

base.update_signal: a drill produces findings, the room or chemistry changes so signage no longer matches, or occupancy of the premises changes

nodes.definition: Log the things that did not hurt anyone — the splash that missed, the unlabelled beaker found on the bench, the alarm that turned out to be a failing sensor, the acid bottle discovered on the cyanide side after a delivery — and treat each as free information about a control that is already failing. Investigate to the control rather than to the person: which obligation class did not hold, why it was possible for it to fail, and what physical or scheduling change, not what promise of greater care, prevents a recurrence. Each correction gets an owner and a verification date, and the loop closes only when someone confirms the change exists in the room. Reporting has to cost the reporter nothing, because in a two-person shop the alternative is a log full of silence and a shop that only ever learns from injuries, which is the most expensive tuition available.

included: near-miss and incident logging with a low-friction format
investigation directed at the failed obligation class
corrective actions expressed as physical or scheduling change with owner and verification date
the no-blame reporting condition
excluded: statutory incident reporting obligations, whose thresholds and forms are jurisdiction-specific and verified from the rule register
disciplinary process and employment decisions
product quality defect analysis, which belongs to the quality specialist

pros.claim: Near misses are frequent, free and predictive, so a shop that logs them sees its control failures long before an injury does
pros.example: three separate reports of unlabelled vessels in one month expose a decanting habit rather than three careless individuals

pros.claim: Requiring a physical or scheduling change stops the comfortable non-fix that closes most small-shop investigations
pros.example: an acid bottle found in the wrong zone results in a delivery-reception point outside both zones rather than a resolution to be careful

cons.claim: In a very small shop the reporter, the investigator and the person who erred are the same person, which makes honest logging psychologically hard
cons.example: the owner who spilled the pickle is the one deciding whether it was worth writing down

cons.claim: Logging without closure creates a record of unfixed problems that is worse than no record when an inspector reads it
cons.example: a log with fifteen open items and no owners documents a pattern of ignoring warnings

failure_modes: closing an investigation with a promise to be more careful
logging only events that caused visible damage
no owner or verification date, so corrections drift indefinitely
using the log as evidence in a competence dispute, which stops reporting immediately
acceptance_tests: a log exists that can be completed in a couple of minutes and shows entries with no injury attached
each entry names the obligation class that failed and a corrective action with an owner and a verification date
closed entries have a recorded confirmation that the change exists in the room
the shop's written stance separates near-miss reporting from competence and authorization review
revisit_triggers: any incident, near miss, drill finding or failed gate item
an open corrective action passing its verification date
a repeat of a previously logged event, which means the correction did not work
a change of personnel that alters who reports and who reviews

base.update_signal: a repeat event shows a correction failed, an open action passes its verification date, or reporting volume falls to zero for an implausible period

nodes.definition: Run every job through a standing pre-run gate that confirms the room is in the state the safety case assumes, because controls are only real on the day they are checked: segregation intact with nothing crossed since the last run, extraction running and its capture verified, the gas detector in date and responding, protective equipment present and sound for the tasks in this job, both spill kits stocked and in their zones, the eyewash route clear, an authorized and trained person on shift with the second-person requirement satisfied where the chemistry demands it, sheets and register reachable, and the pH and level state of every cyanide-bearing vessel known before a lid is lifted. The gate fails closed: any missing item stops the job rather than downgrading it, and the customer conversation about a two-day delay is always cheaper and more honest than the alternative. This is the node where safety outranking throughput stops being a principle and becomes a decision someone actually makes on a Friday afternoon.

included: the pre-run checklist and its fail-closed rule
named halt authority that anyone present can exercise
the record that a gate check happened for this job
routing a failed item into the incident and near-miss log
the customer-communication consequence of a stopped job
excluded: process quality gates such as adhesion, thickness and colour acceptance, which belong to the quality specialist
waste readiness and shipment checks, which belong to the waste knowledge base
claim and marking sign-off before sale, which belongs to the marking knowledge base

pros.claim: A short standing checklist catches the control that silently failed since the last run, which is exactly the failure nobody is looking for
pros.example: the check finds the detector's bump test lapsed while the shop was busy with a large order, before the tank is opened

pros.claim: A fail-closed rule makes the safety-over-throughput dominance concrete and removes the negotiation from a pressured moment
pros.example: a job due tomorrow is postponed because the second trained person called in sick, and the customer is told the real reason

cons.claim: A gate that stops jobs has a direct commercial cost and will be resented on the day it fires
cons.example: a wedding-date order slips by two days because the extraction verification failed, and the shop absorbs the goodwill cost

cons.claim: Checklists decay into ritual signing when they are long or when they never find anything
cons.example: the same nine boxes ticked in ten seconds every morning without anyone walking to look at the eyewash

failure_modes: signing the checklist from the bench without walking the room
downgrading rather than stopping when an item fails, such as running with reduced extraction
the gate owned by one person, so nothing is checked when they are away
failed items resolved quietly and never entering the near-miss log, so the pattern is invisible
acceptance_tests: a completed gate record exists for every job involving hazardous chemistry, naming who checked and when
at least one item on the checklist requires physically walking to and looking at the control rather than recalling it
the written rule states that any failed item stops the job, and names who may halt a run
failed gate items appear in the near-miss log with a corrective action and an owner
revisit_triggers: a gate item fails, or a gate is skipped for any reason
a new chemistry, task or piece of equipment changes what must be checked
an incident that a passing gate did not predict
checklist completion times suggest it is being signed rather than walked

base.update_signal: a gate item fails or is skipped, an incident occurs that the gate did not predict, or the room's chemistry and equipment change what must be verified

edges.why_related: the obligation classes the frame names are exactly what the register must find an owning authority and a proof document for
the frame's rule that no control is derived from memory forces a governed document library as the first physical asset of the safety system
a container may only enter the register once its governing sheet exists, so the library is what makes the register meaningful rather than a list of names
the cyanide hazard picture is only actionable once the shop knows which vessels, including rinses and drag-out, actually carry cyanide-bearing solution
the corrosive hazard picture is sized by which acids and alkalis are held, at what strength and in what quantity
the sensitiser discipline applies only where nickel chemistry is actually present, and the register is what establishes that
which tanks are heated, how large they are and where they sit comes from the register's location and quantity picture
the acid-contact and falling-pH gas mechanisms are the entire reason the segregation line is absolute rather than a good practice
segregation needs both sides of the line characterised, including which acids fume and travel and which are held in bulk
containment and drain design is how the segregation line is made physical for liquids that fall, and it cannot be laid out before the zones are fixed
the mist and vapour routes named in the hazard class are what source capture exists to intercept before the breathing zone
detection is the backstop for extraction failing, so alarm placement and response only make sense once the capture design is known
glove material, breakthrough guidance and eye and body protection are read from the product's own sheet rather than chosen by habit
a label is the register entry made visible on the vessel itself, so labelling has nothing to say until the register exists
an instruction records the method a trained and authorized person was taught, so writing one for chemistry nobody is trained on is improvisation in a document
kit size and the clean-up versus evacuate rule are set by how much a zone can hold and where a spill would travel
the flush is the first step of the written exposure plan, so the plan cannot be honest about the first minute until the provision is real and reachable
the drill rehearses the spill decision rule and the signage carries it, so both need the kits and the rule to exist first
quantity bands, cabinet requirements, licensing and access conditions are jurisdiction-set, so storage design is constrained by whatever the register verified and dated
the alkaline floor below which a free-cyanide solution begins to evolve gas is what turns pH from a process reading into a hard safety constraint with upward-only correction
no readiness gate can pass while any crossing exists between the zones, which makes segregation the gate's first and non-negotiable item
the gate must confirm an authorized trained person is on shift and that the second-person requirement is met, so authorization state constrains whether any job may start
the response to a spill depends entirely on knowing what spilled, so an unlabelled vessel constrains every responder to the worst-case assumption

strong source capture over a hot alkaline bath increases evaporation and the exchange with room air that drives carbonate formation and pH drift, so the control that protects lungs slightly destabilises the solution it sits over
edges.resolution_rule: extraction is never reduced to protect a bath: keep capture at full effect, cover idle tanks, enclose where possible, and absorb the consequence with scheduled make-up, pH logging and analysis per the technical data sheet

edges.why_related: the locked, access-controlled store that keeps cyanide stock secure is exactly the wrong place for the materials someone needs to reach in seconds during a spill
edges.resolution_rule: the lock protects stock, never response materials: spill kits, protective equipment and the sheet pack live outside the locked store, unlocked, in their own zone and near the exit route

edges.why_related: a detector out of calibration, past sensor life or failing its bump test stops the run on precisely the day a promised job is due, which is when the pressure to proceed is highest
edges.resolution_rule: the gate fails closed with no exception: free-cyanide work does not run on an unverified detector, and the job is rescheduled, moved to a non-cyanide route or outsourced while the customer is told the real reason

edges.why_related: the gauntlets and face shield that protect against hot alkaline splash reduce grip and vision on small jewellery over an open hot tank, which raises the chance of the drop that causes the splash
edges.resolution_rule: never downgrade the protection class to regain dexterity: change the handling instead with rack and tong design, lower lift heights, a two-person move or a fixture, and re-test the task with the correct equipment on

edges.why_related: honest near-miss reporting requires that reporting cost the reporter nothing, while authorization exists to withdraw work from people who are not competent, and in a two-person shop those two pressures land on the same individual
edges.resolution_rule: separate the two processes explicitly: near-miss reports feed control redesign and never authorization review, and only a repeated, deliberate breach of a written rule, established outside the log, touches a person's authorization

edges.why_related: a pH excursion below the alkaline floor is the mechanism most likely to make a detector alarm in a shop with no acid crossing, so the alarm is the downstream consequence of this control failing

the unlabelled vessel is the most common causal route by which an acid ends up poured into a cyanide-bearing solution during a routine tidy-up, so labelling failure directly produces segregation failure
hot alkaline splash during withdrawal and transfer is the injury the flush provision is sized and sited against, so this hazard class determines the readiness requirement

sensitisation and dermatitis are the chronic exposures that surface as personal symptoms rather than as incidents, which is what makes the outward routing to occupational health a live path rather than a formality

the sheet is read and its protection, incompatibility and first-aid content extracted before any bench instruction is drafted, because an instruction written from memory hard-codes whatever the shop already got wrong
the written exposure plan exists first and the signage and drills then publish and rehearse it, never the other way round
kits must be stocked, zoned and rule-bound before the gate can meaningfully check them, so readiness is built and then verified job by job
each investigation that finds a task instruction incomplete, ambiguous or outdated returns a concrete edit to the card at the bench, which is how the written method stays connected to the real one
drill performance is the cheapest available evidence of who can actually execute the response, so it feeds refresher training and re-authorization decisions
both are dormant provisions that are only ever needed under stress and both fail in the same three ways — obstructed, depleted and never tested — so they share one verification habit and one drill

conflict_axes.name: readiness_gate_versus_throughput_and_deadline
conflict_axes.description: The pre-run gate stops jobs on the days a shop can least afford it, because control failures do not schedule themselves around promised delivery dates.
poles: run the job to keep the promised date
hold the job until every readiness item is true
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the gate fails closed and the delay is explained honestly to the customer; a job may be rescheduled, re-routed to a lower-hazard chemistry or outsourced, but never run on partial controls

conflict_axes.name: hazard_elimination_versus_hazard_management
conflict_axes.description: A shop can either build and sustain the full control set for cyanide chemistry or eliminate the hazard by choosing a cyanide-free system or sending the plating out, and the middle path of partial controls is the dangerous one.
poles: build controls and run the hazardous chemistry in-house
eliminate or substitute the hazard and give up the in-house capability
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: if any obligation class cannot be satisfied continuously in these premises with these people, eliminate or substitute rather than manage; partial control sets are treated as elimination decisions the shop has not yet made

conflict_axes.name: engineering_controls_versus_protective_equipment_reliance
conflict_axes.description: Protective equipment is visible, cheap and immediately available, while extraction and segregation are expensive and slow to install, so a pressured shop drifts toward wearing its way out of an air or crossing problem.
poles: solve exposure with protective equipment on the person
solve exposure at the source with capture and separation
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: elimination, substitution and engineering come first and protective equipment is added on top; equipment is never accepted as the answer to a vapour, mist or segregation problem

conflict_axes.name: security_lockup_versus_emergency_accessibility
conflict_axes.description: Controlled access protects cyanide stock from theft, misuse and untrained hands, while an emergency needs kits, sheets and protective equipment reachable in seconds by whoever is present.
poles: keep everything needed in an emergency immediately reachable
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: split the two populations: stock and concentrates behind access control, response materials unlocked in their zone near the exit, and the register and sheet pack reachable without a key

conflict_axes.name: open_reporting_versus_authorization_accountability
conflict_axes.description: Learning depends on people reporting their own near misses, while authorization exists to keep work away from those who are not competent, and in a one or two-person shop both land on the same person.
poles: hold individuals accountable for rule breaches
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: route near-miss reports exclusively to control redesign and keep authorization review to repeated deliberate breaches established outside the log

conflict_axes.name: extraction_capture_versus_bath_stability_and_cost
conflict_axes.description: Source capture over hot tanks removes heat and moisture and speeds the room-air exchange that drives pH and carbonate drift, so the breathing-zone control makes the solution slightly harder and more expensive to keep in window.
poles: minimise evaporation, energy loss and bath drift
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: capture is fixed and non-negotiable; recover the cost with lids on idle tanks, partial enclosure, scheduled make-up and more frequent pH and analysis checks

conflict_axes.name: small_shop_affordability_versus_control_completeness
conflict_axes.description: The control set for free-cyanide work has a floor cost in equipment, duplicate kits, monitoring, training and a second person that does not scale down with shop size, however small the tanks are.
poles: scale controls down to what a micro shop can afford
keep the control set whole regardless of shop size
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: controls do not scale below their class floor; the affordable answer is a less hazardous process, a smaller scope of work or outsourcing, never a discounted version of the same control set

conflict_axes.name: self_rescue_impulse_versus_evacuate_and_call
conflict_axes.description: The instinct on an alarm or a bad spill is to shut down the rectifier, save the gold-bearing work and limit the damage, all of which requires staying in the room that just told you to leave.
poles: stay and protect the work and the equipment
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: leaving always wins: no asset, batch or customer commitment justifies remaining in or re-entering the room, and any shutdown steps that matter are engineered to be doable from outside or accepted as lost

conflict_axes.name: class_level_guidance_versus_jurisdiction_specific_numbers
conflict_axes.description: This knowledge base deliberately gives obligation classes and mechanisms while every enforceable figure lives in a local rule or a supplier sheet, which frustrates an operator who wants one number to comply with.
poles: give the class and the pointer and verify the number locally
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: never quote a threshold without its source and date; treat an unanswered numeric question as an open escalation to the named authority or supplier rather than as a gap to fill with a plausible figure

edge_cases.description: A promised job is due today and the gas detector's bump test or calibration has just lapsed
edge_cases.trigger: a readiness item fails on a day with a committed delivery date
edge_cases.mitigation: the gate fails closed, the job is rescheduled or routed to a non-cyanide process or an outside plater, the customer is told the real reason, and the lapse is logged as a near miss with a corrective action on the calibration reminder

edge_cases.description: An unlabelled vessel of clear liquid is found on the bench between the pickle line and the gold line
edge_cases.trigger: a decant or rinse container loses its identity
edge_cases.mitigation: treat it as both worst cases at once: do not smell, test by mixing, pour it into any other vessel or send it to any drain; isolate it in containment in a neutral area, attempt identification only from delivery, decant and log records, and route it to licensed disposal if provenance cannot be established

edge_cases.description: A landlord's plumber arrives to work on the drains and has never been in the room before
edge_cases.trigger: an untrained contractor enters the premises and may connect, cut or flush shared services
edge_cases.mitigation: stop plating work while they are on site, give a recorded induction covering the zones and the alarm response, cover and isolate tanks, state in writing what is present and what must never be connected or flushed, and re-verify the segregation and drain map before the next run

edge_cases.description: Extraction fails or the power drops mid-run with hot tanks live and work in solution
edge_cases.trigger: loss of ventilation or power during an active run
edge_cases.mitigation: follow a pre-agreed stop state: work out of solution if it can be done immediately and safely, current and heaters off, lids on, leave and ventilate the room, and do not resume until capture has been re-verified and the event logged

edge_cases.description: A cyanide-bearing bath left standing over a long weekend reads below its alkaline floor on Monday morning
edge_cases.trigger: one-way pH drift from carbon-dioxide absorption and drag-in during idle time
edge_cases.mitigation: do not open, stir, decant or heat the bath; ventilate the room with detection running, restore pH upward only with the alkali named by the technical data sheet and only by an authorized trained person with a second person present, and log the excursion with a change to the idle-period check routine

edge_cases.description: A solo jeweller wants to finish a cyanide-route job late in the evening with nobody else in the building
edge_cases.trigger: the second-person requirement collides with a one-person operation and a deadline
edge_cases.mitigation: free-cyanide work does not start; the evening is used for non-hazardous bench work and the cyanide step is rescheduled to a staffed slot, because the second trained person is a control and not a convenience

edge_cases.description: The plating room is part of a home or shared building where a family member, cleaner or pet can enter
edge_cases.trigger: non-workers have physical access to the chemistry
edge_cases.mitigation: the room and the store are lockable and locked when unattended, occupants receive the alarm-response induction, and if the space cannot be secured the chemistry class is changed or the work is outsourced rather than accepted with a warning

edge_cases.description: An operator develops a persistent hand rash a few weeks after taking on more nickel underplating work
edge_cases.trigger: a chronic exposure surfaces as a personal symptom rather than as an incident
edge_cases.mitigation: route the person to occupational health or a physician with the relevant sheets and no shop opinion, and separately review glove class, change frequency, mist control and whether a nickel-free stack is appropriate for the work

edge_cases.description: A second-hand tank, pump or heater of unknown history is bought to expand the line
edge_cases.trigger: used equipment enters a room with two chemically incompatible zones
edge_cases.mitigation: assign the item permanently to exactly one zone, mark it indelibly before first use, never share it, and treat any residue in it as unknown hazardous material to be handled through the licensed waste route rather than rinsed out

edge_cases.description: Emergency responders arrive at an incident with no pre-notification, no signage and nobody able to name what is in the tanks
edge_cases.trigger: an incident occurs while the information layer is missing or unreachable
edge_cases.mitigation: keep a sheet pack and the chemical register at the exit so they leave the building with the first person out, put hazard and contact information on the door, and confirm with the local service whether it wants advance notification and record the answer with its date

edge_cases.description: An acid delivery arrives while the corrosive cabinet is already full and the only free lockable space is the cyanide store
edge_cases.trigger: an order exceeds compliant storage capacity
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse or return the excess rather than co-store: order size is capped by cabinet capacity as a written purchasing rule, and the surplus stays with the carrier or is stored compliantly off the premises until capacity exists

workflow.action: Fix the safety frame and keep the decline option on the table
workflow.description: List the obligation classes each intended chemistry family triggers and decide, per family, run here, substitute a lower-hazard system, or outsource
workflow.artifact: obligation-class scope statement with a per-family run, substitute or outsource decision
workflow.gate: every intended chemistry family is matched to its obligation classes and each class is marked satisfied, not yet satisfied, or unsatisfiable in these premises

workflow.description: Name every authority that governs this bench plus landlord and insurer conditions, with the proof document and the date each was verified
workflow.artifact: dated rule-owner register with open questions and who will be asked
workflow.gate: every rule class names an authority, a proof document and a verification date, and no numeric threshold is recorded without its source

workflow.action: Assemble the governing document library before buying anything
workflow.description: Obtain the safety data sheet, and for plating chemistry the technical data sheet, for every product under consideration and index them to the containers they will describe
workflow.artifact: indexed sheet library reachable from the plating room
workflow.gate: no product proceeds to purchase without a current sheet on file in a language the people on shift can read

workflow.action: Register what is actually in the building
workflow.description: Walk the room and record every container, tank, rinse and drag-out vessel with quantity band, location, hazard class and responsible person
workflow.artifact: container-level chemical register including tanks and rinses, with total cyanide-bearing and acid volumes stated
workflow.gate: the walk-round reconciles the register against the room and nothing hazardous is unrecorded, including vessels that look like water

workflow.action: Design the segregation line into the room
workflow.description: Fix the zones, the dedicated equipment sets and the one-way work route before any bench, tank or pump is bought or placed
workflow.artifact: zone plan with dedicated equipment inventory and the work route drawn
workflow.gate: no vessel, tool, pump, glove, tray or spill path is shared between the acid and cyanide zones, and the route never carries acid-wet work over a cyanide vessel

workflow.action: Engineer containment and settle the drains
workflow.description: Walk every vessel's spill path, size secondary containment to the largest credible failure in each zone, and cap or isolate drains in the wet area
workflow.artifact: spill-path map with containment volumes and a recorded drain decision
workflow.gate: each zone's worst credible spill is contained within that zone and no drain is shared between zones

workflow.description: Place incompatible classes apart, put cyanide stock under controlled access with a named holder and a ledger, cap order sizes at storage capacity, and label every vessel including rinses
workflow.artifact: storage plan, access-control and ledger arrangement, and a labelling standard
workflow.gate: incompatible classes are physically separated, cyanide stock is access-controlled and ledgered, and no unlabelled vessel exists in the room

workflow.action: Install and verify the engineering controls
workflow.description: Fit source capture at the tanks, site the discharge away from intakes and neighbours, add detection where free cyanide is run, and open the pH log for every cyanide-bearing vessel
workflow.artifact: control verification log covering capture checks, detector bump tests and pH readings
workflow.gate: capture is demonstrated at the tank, the detector is in date and responds to a bump test, and the pH regime is running before the first live run

workflow.description: Confirm external formal training, sign off competency task by task, publish the authorization list, schedule the second-person rule into the rota, and buy the protective equipment each task's sheet requires
workflow.artifact: training and authorization record with the protective-equipment list per task
workflow.gate: everyone who will touch the chemistry has external training evidence plus in-shop sign-off, the rota satisfies the no-lone-working rule, and no task is scheduled whose protective equipment the shop does not own

workflow.description: Turn the sheets and the trained method into short dated cards at each point of use, with pre-task verifications and explicit stop conditions, pointing at the technical data sheet for any number
workflow.artifact: dated, owned task cards at the bench
workflow.gate: every routine task has a current card naming its protective equipment, its verifications and at least one stop condition, and no card states a setpoint as fact

workflow.action: Stand up emergency readiness and rehearse it
workflow.description: Build one spill kit per zone, write the clean-up versus contain versus evacuate rule, write the exposure plan, prove the eyewash route, put up the signage and run the first drill with everyone on site
workflow.artifact: zoned spill kits, written exposure plan, signage set and a drill record with findings
workflow.gate: kits are zoned and complete, the exposure plan names who calls and what is handed over, the flush route is walked and clear, and the first drill's findings all have owners

workflow.action: Run every job through the pre-run gate
workflow.description: Before each hazardous-chemistry job, walk the room and confirm segregation, capture, detection, protective equipment, kits, flush route, authorization, sheet access and vessel pH and level state
workflow.artifact: completed per-job gate record naming the checker and the time
workflow.gate: the job starts only when every item is true; any failed item stops the job and enters the near-miss log with an owner

dominance_rules.rule: Cyanide and acid segregation dominates every layout, purchasing, cleanup and scheduling decision
dominance_rules.rationale: the failure mode is a rapidly fatal gas rather than a spoiled batch, so no efficiency, cost or convenience argument can be weighed against it
dominance_rules.trigger: any change to room layout, plumbing, equipment, storage or cleaning routine, and any moment a tool or vessel might be used in both zones
dominance_rules.action: block the change or the action until the line is demonstrably intact, and re-walk the zones and spill paths before the next run

dominance_rules.rule: Safety readiness dominates throughput, cost and the customer's date
dominance_rules.rationale: a control that can be suspended for an important job is not a control, and the pressure to suspend it peaks exactly when risk is highest
dominance_rules.trigger: a readiness item fails on a day with a committed delivery or a high-value job in the tank
dominance_rules.action: fail the gate closed, reschedule, re-route or outsource the job, and tell the customer the real reason for the delay

dominance_rules.rule: Elimination and substitution dominate control-building wherever a control class cannot be sustained
dominance_rules.rationale: a partial control set gives the confidence of a complete one without the protection, which is more dangerous than not running the chemistry at all
dominance_rules.trigger: the premises or the people cannot continuously support source capture, detection, lockable storage, containment or a second trained person
dominance_rules.action: move to a lower-hazard chemistry class or outsource the plating rather than run a discounted version of the control set

dominance_rules.rationale: capture and separation work while people are distracted, tired or new, whereas equipment only works when correctly selected, worn and maintained
dominance_rules.trigger: protective equipment is proposed as the answer to a vapour, mist, fume or zone-crossing problem
dominance_rules.action: fix the problem at the source with capture, enclosure or separation and treat the equipment as an addition, never as the solution

dominance_rules.rule: The specific product's safety and technical data sheets dominate habit, memory and any general guidance including this knowledge base
dominance_rules.rationale: hazard classification, incompatibility, protection and operating window are product-specific and change with reformulation
dominance_rules.trigger: a conflict between what the shop has always done and what the sheet says, or a question the sheet does not answer
dominance_rules.action: follow the sheet; where it is silent, ask the supplier in writing and record the answer before proceeding

dominance_rules.rule: Local jurisdiction rules dominate any figure quoted from anywhere else
dominance_rules.rationale: exposure limits, quantity thresholds, licensing and discharge conditions differ by jurisdiction and change over time, and a confident foreign number is indistinguishable from compliance until it is tested
dominance_rules.trigger: a threshold, quantity limit, licence condition or notification requirement is needed for a decision
dominance_rules.action: verify with the named authority, record the answer with its date, and treat an unanswered question as an open escalation rather than a gap to fill

dominance_rules.rule: Evacuate and call dominates asset protection
dominance_rules.rationale: the cost of losing a tank of work, a rectifier or a batch of gold is finite and insurable, while the cost of remaining in a room with an unknown atmosphere is not
dominance_rules.trigger: a gas alarm, a cyanide-zone spill beyond the written size rule, an unexplained odour or symptom, or any unknown-atmosphere event
dominance_rules.action: leave, ventilate, call, and let nobody re-enter for equipment, work or gold until responders or a verified atmosphere permit it

dominance_rules.rule: Professional medical care dominates shop judgement on any exposure or symptom
dominance_rules.rationale: several of these exposure classes present with delay or as chronic sensitisation, and no bench observation can rule them out
dominance_rules.trigger: a splash, an inhalation, a rash, a cough, or any moment someone says they are probably fine
dominance_rules.action: route to emergency services or occupational health with the product sheet, and never diagnose, dose, or clear a person to continue working

dominance_rules.rule: Trained and authorized person rules dominate availability pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: competence and the presence of a second person who can raise an alarm are controls in the same sense that extraction is
dominance_rules.trigger: the only person available is untrained, unauthorized for the task, or would be working alone on free-cyanide chemistry
dominance_rules.action: the task waits for a qualified slot in the rota; it is never run by the nearest available person

dominance_rules.rule: A physical or scheduling change dominates a promise in every incident follow-up
dominance_rules.rationale: the same conditions produce the same event, and intentions are the only corrective action that reliably fails
dominance_rules.trigger: an investigation is about to close with an undertaking to be more careful
dominance_rules.action: require a change to the room, the equipment, the rota or the written instruction, with a named owner and a verification date

anti_rework_rules.rule: Assess the room and settle the chemistry family before buying any chemistry
anti_rework_rules.prevents: owning a free-cyanide system for premises that can never host source capture, secure storage or a second trained person, and then facing licensed disposal of unopened stock

anti_rework_rules.rule: Draw the segregation zone plan before buying or placing tanks, benches, sinks and pumps
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering after the line is plumbed that one sink and one floor drain serve both zones, which means rebuilding the room rather than adjusting a habit

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read the safety data sheet before the order is placed, not when the delivery arrives
anti_rework_rules.prevents: acquiring a product whose storage, protection or licensing obligations the shop cannot meet, and paying twice for the privilege of disposing of it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the maximum order size from cabinet and store capacity before purchasing
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the delivery that has nowhere compliant to go and ends up co-stored with an incompatible class because refusing it felt wasteful

anti_rework_rules.rule: Register and label every container at the moment of delivery or decant
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the unknown-vessel investigation that ends in licensed disposal of a perfectly good chemical, or worse, in someone pouring it into the wrong zone

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify capture at the tank before the first bath is made up
anti_rework_rules.prevents: making up a hot, hazardous bath in a room that then has to be evacuated, cooled and drained because the extraction was never actually tested

anti_rework_rules.rule: Train and authorize people before the first job is scheduled
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the busy-week substitution where an untrained person does the make-up because the work was already promised to a customer

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the task card while the trainer is still present
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reconstructing a method from memory months later and hard-coding a drift that then has to be unlearned by everyone who was taught from it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Prove the emergency readiness before the first live chemistry, not before the first inspection
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering the blocked eyewash, the depleted kit and the flat alarm battery during a real incident instead of during a fifteen-minute drill

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record every jurisdiction answer with its date the first time it is obtained
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-litigating the same licensing question every year and, worse, quoting a stale answer to an inspector as if it were current

iteration_protocol.trigger: an incident or near miss is logged, including a failed readiness-gate item
iteration_protocol.action: investigate to the obligation class that failed, make a physical or scheduling change with an owner and a verification date, update the affected task card, and re-run the readiness checks the event touched

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new product, a new chemistry family or a supplier reformulation enters the shop
iteration_protocol.action: obtain and file the new sheets, update the register, re-derive protection, storage and segregation obligations from the new hazard classes, and reissue the affected cards before the product is used

iteration_protocol.trigger: the room changes: a tank moves, a bench is added, plumbing or flooring work is done, or the shop relocates
iteration_protocol.action: re-walk the zones and every vessel's spill path, re-verify capture, and prove the segregation line intact before the next run

iteration_protocol.trigger: a detector alarms, or a cyanide-bearing solution reads at or below its alkaline floor
iteration_protocol.action: execute the leave-and-ventilate response first, then treat it as an investigation: find the acid path or the drift source, correct upward only by an authorized person with a second present, and tighten the idle-period check routine

iteration_protocol.trigger: a drill or a gate check finds a readiness item missing, blocked, depleted or out of date
iteration_protocol.action: restock or repair immediately, then re-run that specific drill element rather than assuming the fix worked, and log the finding with an owner

iteration_protocol.trigger: headcount or occupancy changes: a new worker, an apprentice, a new tenant, or the loss of the second trained person
iteration_protocol.action: re-check authorization coverage against the task list, re-schedule cyanide work around the second-person rule, and induct everyone who shares the premises

iteration_protocol.trigger: a licence renewal or inspection happens, or the oldest entry in the rule register passes its re-check interval
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify each rule class with its authority, re-date the register, and adjust storage quantities, security and notification arrangements to whatever the current answer is

priority_rationale: The frame nodes come first because the obligation vocabulary, the jurisdiction pointers, the governing sheets and the honest inventory decide what chemistry may exist in this room at all; the hazard classes follow because every control below them is only proportionate once the mechanisms are named; segregation and containment come next because they are physical properties of the premises that cannot be retrofitted around a built line; ventilation, detection, the alkaline pH floor and protective equipment follow as the running controls that keep the day safe; competency, written instruction and emergency readiness come after because they encode who may act and what happens when a control fails; and the readiness gate and the incident loop come last because they are the recurring verification and learning layer that keeps everything above them true on the day a job is actually run.
